inputs.original_text: The owner of Blue Waters has said that Government collects taxes from them “without doing or investing in anything”.Perhaps this might be considered as an environmental tax. Plastic bottles can be found everywhere, blocking rivers and drains, which then enter...
inputs.modified_text: The owner of Blue Waters is right to question a government that taxes people while plastic waste continues to choke rivers and drains. But this cannot be reduced to whether individuals respect public spaces: businesses and institutions help shape the systems that produce and manage waste, and responsibility should not be shifted onto ordinary people alone. Any environmental tax must come with transparent accountability and real investment in services that protect everyone, especially communities left to live with the consequences of pollution.
